verdict: Spotify grew revenue 8% to €4.53B (about $5.24B) — 14% in constant currency — and a €184M one-off gain on its exchangeable notes helped lift net income to €721M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago (+14% in constant currency)

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Paid subscriptions — the engine of the business. Revenue up 10% YoY in euros (€4,148M as reported) with 293M subscribers.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising revenue. Down 5% YoY in euros (€385M as reported) as ad demand softened.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the app, recommendation systems and new formats like video podcasts and audiobooks (€331M as reported).

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning listeners and advertisers (€342M as reported).

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day (€107M as reported); lower this quarter as share-price-linked social charges fell.

follow100Note: Premium subscriptions are about $92 of every $100 Spotify takes in; the free tier is the funnel, not the engine. Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
otherDetail: Finance items netted a gain of €222M as reported: finance income of €248M — including a €184M fair-value gain on the Exchangeable Notes and €52M of interest income — minus €26M of finance costs, which included €18M of foreign-exchange losses.
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.1551 (USD:Euro 0.8657 at Mar 31, 2026, the rate in Spotify's own release), with small rounding adjustments so the converted lines foot exactly. As reported: revenue €4,533M · gross profit €1,495M · operating income €715M · net income €721M.

takeaways.title: Constant-currency growth accelerated
takeaways.text: Reported revenue rose 8% to €4,533M, held back by currency moves; in constant currency it grew 14%. Premium subscribers rose 9% to 293M and monthly users reached 761M, both ahead of guidance.

takeaways.title: A notes gain padded the bottom line
takeaways.text: Finance income included a €184M fair-value gain on Spotify's Exchangeable Notes, which were then settled and taken off the balance sheet during the quarter. Even without it, operating income rose 40% to €715M on a 33.0% gross margin.

takeaways.title: Cash flow stayed very strong
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was €824M in the quarter, taking the last-twelve-months total to €3.2B, while operating cash flow was €836M.

oneTimers: Fair-value gain on Exchangeable Notes: €184M inside finance income — a non-cash gain recorded before the notes were settled and derecognized in the quarter (a €1,304M cash settlement).
